reviews.reason: Administrator session and current database role are required. A stopped-writer attestation and actor-bound exact snapshot authorize only a bounded batch of processing retries with both claim fields absent. Retry/source locks, source versions, attempt preservation, derived item state and a unique audit receipt share one transaction; provider scheduling is post-commit only.
reviews.followUp: Keep real PostgreSQL stale-review, concurrent confirmation, quota preservation, rollback and lost-reply tests current. This is operator-attested recovery, not proof that an old unfenced binary stopped or authority to replace partial/current claims.

reviews.reason: Independent retries atomically claim a single due row with a UUID and deadline. Durable dependency cooldowns can only postpone admission. Provider helpers return evidence only; availability is checked before each request. Result transactions lock the received claim, check expiry after lock acquisition and before commit, verify the source and active movie/TV library, and save metadata, fallback or outcome, due time, cooldown and item state together. The dispatcher processes bounded batches and does not grant write authority. Recovery uses bounded locked expired claims; no missing legacy ownership is inferred.
reviews.followUp: Keep real PostgreSQL competing consumer, late provider, crash recovery, source-change, fallback rollback and lost-commit-reply tests current. This is cooperative retry fencing, not certification of shared caches, other enrichment callers, legacy writers or routing effects.

reviews.reason: Metadata-enrichment tasks lock and recheck their received queue claim and database-clock deadline for database-only writes. Final metadata, source-library history, completion and item state share a checked-out transaction. Source snapshots and provider recovery leases remain additional guards; fallback retries notify the existing scheduler only after commit.
reviews.followUp: Keep real PostgreSQL expiry, replacement, lock-wait and rollback tests current. Other classification, rating, independent retry workers and shared provider caches are not certified by this boundary; no exactly-once or ingestion ownership claim is made.

reviews.reason: The bounded metadata relay locks a completed ingestion generation and commits queue inserts, derived enrichment state and cursor together. Candidate eligibility and the ordinary-pass exclusion prevent that pass from bypassing pending handoff demand. No pruning, provider request or routing is authorized.
reviews.followUp: Keep rollback, concurrent relay, legacy adoption, generation replacement and process-death-before-enqueue tests current. This context does not certify arbitrary shared enrichment callers, old binaries or external writers.

reviews.reason: Content-page admission uses the current ingestion owner's checked-out connection. Revision and epoch fencing, a session-scoped recovery probe and durable pre-request charging coordinate source outages without weakening library ownership, pruning or learning gates.
reviews.followUp: Keep real HTTP and PostgreSQL coverage for all providers, concurrent healthy imports, 100-library outages, probe contention, owner loss, stale success, Retry-After and independent-source isolation. This does not coordinate unrelated metadata clients or legacy external writers.

reviews.reason: Catalog-only recovery shares one session lock across manual and automatic reconciliation. Durable admission, diagnostics and the additive configuration-fenced merge stay on the checked-out owner connection. Retry budgets never grant ingestion, pruning, archive or learning authority.
reviews.followUp: Keep real provider outage, persisted cooldown, Retry-After, ownership loss, credential revision, upgrade and ingestion-readiness integration checks current. Older external writers do not participate in this cooperative catalog lock.

reviews.reason: Bounded discovery status writes are attempt/configuration fenced and best-effort, with sanitized provider reasons. Completion follows the existing non-deleting merge; diagnostics grant no ingestion ownership, archive approval or routing authority.
reviews.followUp: Keep Jellyfin/Emby/Plex contracts, configuration ABA, overlapping attempts, persistence failures and fresh/upgrade schema tests current. An unfinished observation never proves a worker has stopped.

reviews.reason: Read-only provider-specific catalog negotiation validates bounded complete pages before exposing a result to the source-fenced, non-deleting reconciler. No identity remapping or data deletion is authorized.
reviews.followUp: Keep current/legacy HTTP fixtures, later-page failures, cancellation and no-partial-write PostgreSQL tests current. Stable offset totals do not prove an atomic source snapshot.

reviews.reason: Catalog discovery is additive and source-configuration fenced. Archive uses the ingestion owner lock, disabled-state constraint, exact admin review and atomic audit; it never deletes inventory.
reviews.followUp: Keep reduced catalogs, malformed envelopes, archive rollback, restore-disabled and owner contention integration evidence current. This does not certify legacy external writers.

reviews.reason: Read-only ingestion predicates, status and readiness expose pending legacy adoption and unfinished markers. Watchdog selection never grants ownership; MediaSync revalidates under its session lock.
reviews.followUp: Keep populated legacy adoption, hidden foreign markers, disabled configuration, first full replay and post-completion exclusion covered by real PostgreSQL tests. Read-side eligibility is not proof that historical external writers stopped.

reviews.reason: Current MediaSyncService entry path uses per-library advisory ownership and the same leased connection for checkpoint and completion writes. This classification is scoped to that entry path, not arbitrary callers.
reviews.followUp: Keep source-enumeration, session-loss, late callback, source-change and atomic-pruning integration evidence current; do not treat cooperative locks or provider counts as storage enforcement or an atomic upstream snapshot.

reviews.reason: Administrator reconciliation uses the common owner lock, locked rows, current-admin, exact-revision and stopped-worker checks with an atomic audit receipt. Default maintenance requires a disabled library; explicit resume requires an already enabled/configured supported source and library. Neither changes settings nor proves old writers stopped.
reviews.followUp: Preserve explicit old-worker shutdown attestation; test mode-bound receipts, revision races, lock contention, audit rollback and outage-to-backfill handoff. Cooperative exclusion does not authorize autonomous recovery of unknown historical writers.

reviews.reason: Existing direct or dynamic write candidates outside the reviewed ingestion entry path. Shared helpers and other workflows are not proven to acquire ingestion ownership.
reviews.followUp: Trace callers and isolate destructive capture/pruning behind explicit owned capabilities before claiming coordinated compatibility.

reviews.reason: Existing indirect query arguments or dynamic execution remain outside static data-flow proof. These entries freeze current coverage gaps, not confirmed unsafe writes.
reviews.followUp: Review changes and resolve query targets and caller coordination; retain an explicit gap when analysis cannot prove the target.

reviews.reason: SQL schema and migration sources may include triggers, functions and cascades outside static DML proof. Pin all SQL history without authorizing concurrent execution.
reviews.followUp: Review schema/migration changes together with restore and upgrade tests; separately assess deployed privileges and database-enforced fencing.

reviews.reason: Offline maintenance and prototype sources can contain direct or indirect writers. Their lifecycle is not proven compatible with active ingestion.
reviews.followUp: Keep maintenance isolated from live ingestion; review target databases, coordination and test-only boundaries before any changed execution.
